input.message:
Fact-check of /home/user/ainews/data/2026-09-28.script.json against /home/user/ainews/data/2026-09-28.json. Discrepancies, most serious first.

1. FABRICATED DETAIL — skill-cascading worked example (NeurIPS item)
Script (B): "One skill weakens the signal for discontinued medications, a second downgrades the severity of the resulting drug interaction, a third suppresses the low-priority alert."
Edition (only text on this): "Its worked example is a prescription-review pipeline in which three separately innocuous skill edits combine to make a severe drug-interaction warning 'silently disappear before reaching the physician'."
The three specific skill mechanics are nowhere in the edition. Invented.

2. UNSUPPORTED CLAIM — MIT Tech Review item
Script (A): "None of this month's agent episodes comes close."
Edition says only that MITTR is "the only outlet we found making this specific comparison between the incident definitions and this month's agent episodes", plus Arnold's quote. The edition never states that no episode meets the threshold.

3. DROPPED CAVEAT — MIT Tech Review item
Edition bullet 4: "The thresholds are the reported text of the statutes as MIT Technology Review describes them; we did not open the bills themselves."
The script keeps MITTR attribution and the single-source flag but drops the "we did not open the bills" caveat entirely — notable given the intro/outro both promise "where a page wouldn't open for us, we say so".

4. DROPPED SCOPE QUALIFIER — Nvidia item
Script (B): "Nvidia says the chip sits on the node's only path to the model."
Edition: "in Vera Rubin POD systems the BlueField-4 DPU sits on 'the node's only path to the model'". The script generalises a claim the edition confines to Vera Rubin POD systems.

5. ADDED TIMING + IMPLIED RESPONSE — Gates/Trump item
Script (A): "The President's answer, to Fox News the same day: ..."
Edition: "Trump, speaking to Fox News at the Presidents Cup, reaffirmed his opposition to slowing down". The edition gives no date for the Fox News remarks and does not frame them as an answer to Gates.

6. CAUSAL FRAMING NOT IN EDITION — MIT Tech Review item
Script (B): "And here's why that's happening in Canberra rather than Sacramento."
Nothing in the edition links the Australian hearing to the weakness of US state thresholds.

7. CAVEAT NARROWED IN INTRO
Script (B, intro): "only require reporting above 50 deaths or $1 billion in damage."
Edition summary: "more than 50 deaths or physical injuries or $1 billion in damage". "or physical injuries" is dropped (it survives in the later item block).

8. NUMBER SOFTENED / NAME ADDED — VSMC item
Script (A): "the 99% first-lot yield" vs edition "the first sample lot yielded above 99%".
Script (B): "VSMC, the Vanguard and NXP joint venture" — the edition only says "VIS holds 60 percent and NXP 40 percent"; "Vanguard" appears nowhere in the item.

9. COMPANY CLAIM STATED AS FACT — Holo4 item
Script (A): "What they do offer is every trajectory behind the public benchmark scores."
Edition: "H says its ... it open-sources 'every trajectory behind our scores on public benchmarks'" — an attributed company claim in an item flagged company-claim.

10. ATTRIBUTION SHIFT — Australia item
Script (B): "OpenAI says it only learned of it in August, that it was one of at least four Australian government sites, ..."
Edition: "OpenAI says it only learned of the breach — one of at least four Australian government websites — in August" — "one of at least four" is the edition's own aside, not something OpenAI is said to have said.

11. ADDED CHARACTERISATION — CoT-monitor item
Script (B): "train a reasoning model on a main task plus a hidden side task" (edition: "a main task plus a side task"), and "The worry going in was that the model would hide its reasoning in code no one can read" — the edition states the surprising finding but never describes a prior expectation.

12. ADDED DETAIL — MIT vaccine item
Script (A): "used a machine-learning method built for small datasets". Edition says "machine-learning optimisation" and cites the paper title "data-efficient AI"; "built for small datasets" is the script's own gloss.

13. TERM SWAPS (minor)
- "Billing codes managed an F1 of 0.78" — edition calls them ICD codes / "diagnostic codes", not billing codes.
- "BlueField-4 network chips" (intro and item) for the edition's "BlueField-4 DPUs".
- MITTR item: "A policy researcher quoted in the piece" — edition identifies Mackenzie Arnold of the Institute for Law and AI; the role label is the script's.

14. DROPPED SOURCING DETAIL — FT item
Script (B): "A Financial Times analysis found mentions ... running about six times higher than the same period last year."
Edition: the sixfold figure is AlphaSense data, for August and September, covering earnings calls "and in investor meetings", per ChainCatcher's summary. The script drops AlphaSense, the window and investor meetings, and states it as an FT finding (the second-hand caveat does survive later in the block).

No discrepancies found in: Holo4 benchmark numbers (61.7 / 81.8 / 30.9, reference-score provenance), CoT-monitor figures (63%, 1/10, second run, paraphrasing), 89.4% / 24 configurations / 213 test cases, JADEPUFFER numbers and credential route and "covered on Saturday" (26 Sep 2026 = Saturday), China sequence and 15 September date, MIT vaccine temperatures / ~50 excipients / five / mice / Nature Biotechnology, cardiac-arrest metrics and 45,525 cohort, Australia names/date/written-requests caveat, Gates quotes, VSMC 44,000 wafers / Q1 2027 / 1,600 / 130–40nm / interposer customers, AT&T 40%/70%/45bn tokens and Tinder $1m→$10m. The ScopeBench, Game Arena, KNOWS, stale-document, ESET, Taiwan, Kyivstar and IDIBELL items are simply omitted, which is not a discrepancy.

input.message:
Second-round check of /home/user/ainews/data/2026-09-28.script.json against /home/user/ainews/data/2026-09-28.json. Most numbers, names, quotes and attributions now reconcile (Holo4 61.7/30.9/81.8, 89.4% ASR + 24 configs + 213 cases, 63% @1/10, JADEPUFFER 16h/300+/100+/~7min, 45,525 encounters / 0.88 / 1.00 / 0.94 / 0.79 / 0.78, 44,000 wpm / Q1 2027 / 130–40nm / >99%, AT&T 40%→70% / 45bn tokens / Tinder $1m→$10m, Sept 15 exit-entry rules, 50 deaths / $1bn, partner lists, all quotations). The following do not.

1. Dropped statutory trigger (item block, MITTR)
Script: "California's SB 53, New York's RAISE Act and Illinois's SB 315 define a reportable critical safety incident as one causing more than 50 deaths or physical injuries, or $1 billion in damage."
Edition bullet: "...more than 50 deaths or physical injuries, or $1 billion in damage — plus cases where a model deceives its developers outside an evaluation in a way that materially increases catastrophic risk."
The script presents the harm thresholds as the whole definition and drops the second trigger. (The intro's version of this is fine — it tracks the `summary` field, which also omits the clause.)

2. Overstated defence result (CoT-monitor item)
Script: "the defence is almost mundane: paraphrase the chain of thought first, and the same monitor catches it again."
Edition: "paraphrasing increases mean Suspicion Score from 2.5 and 1.2 to 7.4 in both runs, with approximately 70% of paraphrased samples receiving scores of 10. Main task performance is retained at 91% for Run A and 63% for Run B."
"Catches it again" reads as full restoration; the edition's figures are partial (~70% at 10/10, mean 7.4), and the main-task cost (63% for Run B) is dropped.

3. "Not peer reviewed" contradicts the edition's own detail (CoT-monitor item)
Script: "It's a preprint, not peer reviewed, and a single source."
Edition: comments field says "23 pages, 6 figures. Accepted at the AdvML-Frontiers x CoTMA Workshop at COLM 2026." The edition flags it "preprint" but never says "not peer reviewed", and records a workshop acceptance.

4. Attribution of the hearing date (Australia item)
Script: "CNBC, carrying Reuters, reports that Sam Altman and Dario Amodei have been sent written requests ... in Canberra on Thursday, October 1st."
Edition: "CNBC, carrying Reuters, reported ... public hearings in Canberra on Thursday. The Greens media release from chair Sarah Hanson-Young gives the date as Thursday 1 October." The specific date is the Greens release's, not CNBC/Reuters'. Same item: script calls her "Senator Sarah Hanson-Young"; the edition only calls her the inquiry's chair (Australian Greens).

5. Unsupported ranking (CoT-monitor item)
Script: "it's the most uncomfortable result of the day."
No edition text ranks items; this item's `impact` is "mixed". Nothing in the item's headline or bullets supports a superlative across the edition.

6. Unsupported characterisation (transition before the China item)
Script: "To the geopolitics, and an export control aimed at people rather than hardware."
The edition describes exit-approval / overseas-travel restrictions and State Council Exit-Entry Management regulations; it never characterises them as an export control (a `topics` tag is not edition text).

7. Unsupported comparative (transition before health)
Script: "To health and science, where the results today are quieter and better documented."
The edition's health items are flagged variously (`preprint`, `single-source` for the medRxiv item) and it makes no comparison of documentation quality between sections.

8. Hedge dropped from a quotation (Gates/Trump item)
Script: "we're about a year and a half up on China."
Edition quote: "We're about maybe a year and a half up on China."

9. Intensifier added (CoT-monitor item)
Script: "A second run didn't transfer at all."
Edition: "a second training run's behaviour did not transfer, with 80% of samples scored 10/10" — i.e. 20% were not scored 10/10; "at all" is stronger than the edition.

10. Minor qualifier drops (VSMC item)
Script: "headcount goes to around 1,600" — edition: "headcount reaches around 1,600 at full capacity" (current headcount ~1,000, omitted).
Script: "the chairman saying demand for power management and analog parts, particularly for data centres" — edition: "VIS chairman Fang Leuh" (not VSMC's), and "particularly for industrial applications and data centers".

11. Sourcing boilerplate overstates the edition (intro/outro)
Script: "Every claim here is linked on the site" / "with a link to every source behind every claim we've made."
Edition (China item): "Bloomberg's own page would not open from this session ... so it is not linked here"; likewise reuters.com and ft.com are not linked. The paired "where a page wouldn't open for us, we say so" mitigates but does not reconcile the absolute claim.
